sources.title: Global Switch announcement: Global Switch selected to host one of Europe's largest NVIDIA Blackwell deployments in Paris (29 September 2026)
sources.publisher: Global Switch
sources.source_family: Global Switch announcements and data-centre pages
sources.summary: Global Switch's announcement dated 29.09.26 states in the present tense that Global Switch's Paris data centre provides a highly connected, NVIDIA DGX-Ready platform for AI, HPC and enterprise deployments; that it has been selected to host one of the largest NVIDIA Blackwell deployments in Europe, which will be majority liquid-cooled and hosted within that data centre; and that the Paris site is powered by 100% renewable energy and is an approved participant in the European Code of Conduct for Energy Efficiency in Data Centres. The President of Global Switch France is quoted on established, highly connected data centres. The release adds that Global Switch has recently undertaken a heat-offtake agreement for the Levallois-Perret district heating network, set for delivery in 2027 and soon to be replicated in Clichy, and its boilerplate says the company operates carrier- and cloud-neutral data centres in Europe and Asia-Pacific. The Blackwell deployment itself is described as forthcoming and is not treated as installed.
sources.date_semantics: Release dated 29.09.26 on the page; structured data give datePublished 2026-09-29T08:55:51Z and dateModified 2026-10-06T09:01:36Z. The modification falls 30 minutes after Global Switch published its 25-years announcement (2026-10-06T08:31Z), whose related-content teaser repeats the same present-tense sentence under the 29.09.26 date. No Internet Archive copy exists (Wayback availability API, 26 October 2026), so the 6 October modification date is not used; the observation is the publication date. The forthcoming deployment, the 2027 heat delivery and the Clichy replication are forecasts.

sources.publisher: Digital Realty Trust
sources.source_family: Digital Realty website (blog, facility and project pages)
sources.summary: Digital Realty's blog post dated 13 October 2026 states that, through Interxion, now part of Digital Realty, it has operated in Paris for more than 25 years, and that in Paris its Digital Enterprise Hub comprises 14 strategically located data centres surrounding the city, empowering businesses to deploy critical infrastructure. It says that at the hub's core is the Paris Digital Park in La Courneuve, one of France's largest data-centre campuses, featuring four interconnected data centres (PAR8, PAR9, PAR10 and PAR11), 40,000 m2 of IT space, 80 MW of IT capacity and EUR 1.2 billion invested since 2020, with PAR10 featuring native direct liquid cooling; that it matches 100% of the electricity used by its French data centres with renewable energy sourced in France; and that ISO 27001 and PCI-DSS certifications apply across all its data centres in France. It adds that Digital Realty is expanding its Paris footprint with the Dugny Digital Hub (PAR15, PAR16 and PAR17; more than 65,000 m2 of IT space and 176 MW of IT capacity planned), whose construction began in 2025 with the first facility targeted for delivery in 2027.

sources.title: Sesterce newsroom: Rovaltain Becomes a Sesterce Campus (Valence, 6 October 2026)
sources.publisher: Sesterce Group
sources.summary: Sesterce's release datelined Valence, France, 6 October 2026 states that Sesterce's Rovaltain project in Alixan is becoming a Sesterce Campus built around six commitments (architecture, new renewable capacity, cooling without drinking water, jobs, spaces open to residents and a EUR 10 million local fund paid at commissioning). It reaffirms a strict 40 MW limit for the supercomputer, says the campus designed by Patriarche will be revised to integrate these principles (energy, water, noise, landscape, biodiversity, mobility and backup generators), and states that implementation of the building permit already obtained is suspended while these commitments are integrated. It proposes a local dialogue committee with local authorities and associations and a charter to be submitted to Valence Romans Agglo. Sesterce describes itself as designing, building and operating supercomputer campuses.

sources.summary: The municipality republishes NYAB's release of 9 October 2026: NYAB Finland Oy has signed a contract for the preparatory works of the first phase of the data-centre campus planned in Utajärvi, developed by Data Tank Nordic Oy, the project company of AMP Tank AG; the works start immediately; the contract covers site-preparation and infrastructure works required for the campus, with options to extend the preparatory works, and its value is not disclosed. The municipal manager is quoted calling the start of construction works another concrete step in developing the campus.

sources.title: Utajärven kunta, Lupa- ja valvontalautakunta: pöytäkirja 14.04.2026 § 16, Rakentamislupa 26-0014-RL (Data Tank Nordic Oy)
sources.publisher: Utajärven kunta (Municipality of Utajärvi)
sources.summary: The permit and supervision board's minutes of 14 April 2026, § 16 (case 54/10.03.00/2026), approve building permit 26-0014-RL for applicant Data Tank Nordic Oy on building site 889-407-0004-0131 (property Tietomaa, 263,910 m2; detailed plan of 2024; the project complies with the plan) at Prosessitie 2, 91600 Utajärvi: a substation, battery storage, backup generators, a control building and four data-centre buildings, RAK 1 22,476 m2 / 189,340 m3, RAK 2 to RAK 4 21,300 m2 / 184,250 m3 each and RAK 5 368 m2 / 1,710 m3, 86,744 m2 and 743,800 m3 in all. The battery storage is 200/400 MW and the backup generators' fuel power is under 50 MW.
